scope: R193: direct measurement confirms FA carries about 47 percent per-tile fixed overhead, without a profiler

how_the_profiler_was_bypassed.problem: R192 found device profiling unsupported on this chip
how_the_profiler_was_bypassed.insight: the five R191 configurations are themselves a controlled experiment: their total flops are nearly identical at 3.444-3.467 TFLOP (under 1 percent apart) while the time spans 142.00 to 254.98 ms, an 1.8x spread
how_the_profiler_was_bypassed.therefore: with the arithmetic held constant, the spread can only come from how the work is chopped, that is from per-tile cost

fit.excluded_point: br=64/bc=304 does not fit the same line because changing br alters the q-block structure, a different variable

confirms_r190.r190_status: arithmetic inference from cube 24 percent, vector at most 21 percent, HBM 23 percent all being low at once
confirms_r190.now: independent measured confirmation that the time is governed by tile count at constant flops
confirms_r190.verdict: the bubble / fixed-overhead hypothesis now has direct evidence, not just inference

implications_for_10s.note: exceeds the 1.50x the 10 s target needs

implications_for_10s.conclusion: the FA 1.5x is reachable by attacking per-tile overhead, which turns FA from an open question into a scoped engineering problem

directions_from_the_fit.formula: T = 83.5 ms + 2.922 us * tiles, so there are two multiplicative levers
directions_from_the_fit.lever_1_reduce_tiles: Bc=384 already drops tiles from 24858 to 19665 and yields 142.00 ms (1.089x); Bc=768 would halve the tiles again and is projected near 112 ms (1.38x), but UB capacity bounds Bc and that needs checking
directions_from_the_fit.lever_2_reduce_per_tile_cost: lower the 2.922 us coefficient via pipeline overlap and double buffering, interleaving the cube and vector phases with K/V prefetch
directions_from_the_fit.combination: halving both gives about 97.9 ms, roughly 1.58x, which clears the target

limits: fitted on four points at one shape (B=1 H=7 N=41792 D=128), not validated across shapes
the 83.53 ms intercept is an extrapolation to zero tiles, not an attainable floor; the real floor is bounded by the 1.44 us per-tile cube work
the 47 percent applies to the current baseline configuration and will move with the config
changing the tile alters accumulation order, so it remains numerically non-equivalent and can never be a candidate without approval
